Mars Pathfinder and Sojourner (NASA): landed 4 July 1997 in Ares Vallis using airbags; Sojourner was the first Mars rover. Nozomi (Japan, 1998): failed to enter Mars orbit (2003). Mars Climate Orbiter (NASA): lost on 23 September 1999 because of an English/metric unit mismatch in ground software. Mars Polar Lander and Deep Space 2 (NASA): lost on 3 December 1999. # Knowledge base: mars_planet.md / Orbit, day and year
excerpt: Semi-major axis 1.524 AU (227.9 million km); eccentricity 0.0934; perihelion 1.381 AU, aphelion 1.666 AU. Sidereal rotation 24 h 37 m 22.7 s. Solar day (sol) 24 h 39 m 35.2 s = 1.0275 Earth days. Orbital period 686.98 Earth days = about 668.6 sols. NeuroNexus' MY34 dust scenario has 668 daily (sol) bins. Obliquity (axial tilt) 25.19°, so Mars has seasons; its obliquity varies chaotically over millions of years (roughly 15°–45°), which drives ice-age-like climate cycles. Earth–Mars distance ranges from about 55 million km (close opposition) to about 400 million km (solar conjunction). One-way light time is ≈ 3 to 22 minutes. Synodic period (Earth–Mars alignment repeat) ≈ 780 days (~26 months): launch windows and solar conjunctions recur on this cadence. During solar conjunction (~2 weeks) commanding is suspended. excerpt: Hope / Emirates Mars Mission (UAE, built and operated by MBRSC): orbit 9 February 2021; studies global weather and the diurnal cycle from a high orbit. Perseverance / Mars 2020 (NASA): landed 18 February 2021 in Jezero crater, an ancient lake with a river delta. It is caching rock cores for possible future return. The "Cheyava Falls" rock (2024) shows features that are candidate potential biosignatures; these are not confirmed evidence of life. Ingenuity Mars Helicopter: the first powered, controlled flight on another planet, on 19 April 2021. It made 72 flights before rotor damage ended its mission in January 2024. # Knowledge base: mars_missions.md / 1990–1999
excerpt: Mars Observer (NASA): lost in August 1993, days before orbit insertion. Mars Global Surveyor (MGS, NASA): orbit September 1997, operated until November 2006. Carried MOLA (laser altimeter — the global topography NeuroNexus uses), TES, MOC camera and magnetometer. Ingenuity Mars Helicopter: the first powered, controlled flight on another planet, on 19 April 2021. It made 72 flights before rotor damage ended its mission in January 2024. Synodic period (Earth–Mars alignment repeat) ≈ 780 days (~26 months): launch windows and solar conjunctions recur on this cadence. During solar conjunction (~2 weeks) commanding is suspended.
